Chain Shortening Calculator
Result
Pitch per link is looked up from chain diameter (8/10/13/16/19/22/26mm), same table as the reference shortening calculator. Links to remove is rounded to the nearest whole link, so the actual shortened amount can land a few mm off the target — that's the "Difference from Target" figure below. "Top Down" is the same measurement this tool has always used (current minus desired length); where the total chain length is known, the same physical cut point is also given as "Bottom Up" — whichever direction is fewer links is marked quicker to count. Always cross-check against the chain's own data plate/certification before cutting.

All Four Legs — Reference Frames
Outrigger If Moved
from current position		 If Left in Place
from new center		 Baseline
standard target offset
MUST MOVE = its current spot would sit under the crane's own chassis once this shift is complete, checked per leg against the actual footprint and shift — not just which side of the crane it's on, so a diagonal shift can require a front or rear leg to move too. Optional legs don't need to move, but "If Moved" still shows where their standard spot would be if you choose to relocate them anyway — and flags NOT POSSIBLE if that spot is currently under the crane's own chassis, before it moves. On the site plan, the blue outlined dot for an optional leg shows that same target spot.
Bog Mat Marking (from edge of crane, for laying the mat out on the ground)
▶ How O/R % Marking Works (animated walkthrough)
Outrigger To Pad Center Inside Edge
closer to crane		 Outside Edge
further from crane
Measured laterally from the crane's own side (carrier edge, not centerline) out to the pad — mark the inside edge first, then the outside edge, to lay the mat out square before the crane arrives. Only shown for legs with a pad currently toggled on above, using that leg's current (possibly shifted) position — same OEM-sourced span figures as Crane Layout's own ground layout marks, so a mirrored pair (e.g. C2/C3) always reads the same distance from the edge when unshifted.

"O/R %" (Outrigger Reading, shown for cranes with a confirmed support plate size) works out the no-load outrigger extension that puts the support plate's own outer edge — not just the outrigger's own centerline reach — exactly on that mm mark, so it can be paint-marked before the outrigger is ever fully extended. Rounded to the nearest whole percent (whichever is physically closest to the target mm mark, typically within a couple of centimetres) — real on-site adjustment only happens in whole-percent steps anyway. Never a load-rated position — the crane only ever lifts from its own published support stages.

Layout Dimensions
Same paint-out-on-soil figures as the 3D preview's "Show ground layout marks" toggle above, as plain numbers. Forward/back is measured from the slew centre along the carrier's own centerline; out from edge is measured from the carrier's own side (not centerline) — the reference a crew actually measures from in the field.
Outrigger Fwd/Back Out From Edge
½ carrier width (rear, C1 side):
360° Slew Clearance
Point Radius
from slew center		 Clearance
beyond side of carrier
Side clearance assumes the crane is parked with its centerline parallel to whatever it needs to clear (wall, stockpile, fence, etc.) — the true worst case, since at that parking angle the swing radius becomes pure sideways distance. Park at an angle to the structure and the real clearance is larger than shown here. Rear clearance assumes the crane is backed square up to whatever sits directly behind it, measured from the rear of the carrier chassis (or the box's own rear face, once fitted, straight back to each radius point — cranes with a removable rear box show both fitted and not-fitted figures side by side). Carrier width is this fleet's standard 525/80 R25 tyre (see the crane operating instructions, chapter 1.03, for other tyre options) except where noted. Reference tool only — cross-check against the current OEM documentation and the actual site before slewing near a structure.

Crane & Boom Configuration
Reeving 1-way
Pinch to zoom, drag to pan, double-tap to reset
Diagrams are the actual OEM reeving plan artwork (doc. 98036716), extracted directly — not redrawn. Leading number = winch (1 or 2). Each token is a sheave position with a face suffix — f = boom-head front face, r = boom-head rear face (cab side); bare numbers are hook-block sheave positions. F = rope dead-ends at the fixed anchor point. Cross-check against the current rigging plan before use on site.

Driving Configuration
Figures shown are for this fleet's standard 525/80 R 25 tyres — see the crane operating instructions, chapter 1.03, for other tyre options. "Maximum known size hook block" is the heaviest block from this crane's own fleet spec that fits the Hook block allowance above it — a ceiling, not a suggestion to swap blocks. Site clearance limit for how far the counterweight tray can swing out — any configuration needing more radius than this is excluded, since it wouldn't physically fit on your site.
Site Rules & Rigging Weight
Both the printed chart capacity AND the target load you enter are for reference only until rigging weight is accounted for — per the OEM load chart manual ("40.02 Basic information"), the weight of load lifting equipment and fastening equipment must be deducted from the chart's capacity, since it hangs from the boom tip before your actual load is even attached. Selecting a block here (and Winch 2's, if fitted) applies that deduction automatically.
Top Options
Scope: T-boom only (no lattice/folding jib), outriggers fully deployed (7.9m x 8.3m rear / 7.0m front), 360° slewing range. Radius is rounded up to the nearest tabulated chart row — see the notice above when that happens. Reference tool only — cross-check the shown chart code/reference against the current OEM load chart before lifting.
Cranes to Compare
Target
No rigging weight deduction here (hook block/Winch 2 vary per crane) — target load is checked straight against each crane's chart capacity. Each crane finds its own minimum counterweight and best-margin boom configuration, at that crane's default wind bracket and ballast radius (widest/most permissive where applicable) — switch to Find Boom Configuration for full control over a single crane. "Road legal CWT" only affects cranes with a confirmed road-legal counterweight figure (currently the LTM 1110 and LTM 1130) — everything else falls back to the full chart, same as when this is off.

LTM 1650-8.1 Jib Assembly
Assembly Drawing
Pinch to zoom, drag to pan when zoomed in. Double-tap to zoom in/out.
Section Kit List
Codes are read directly off the OEM assembly drawing above (dwg 98035472 / 98036881) — that drawing is the reference, cross-check against the image if in doubt. On the luffing jib, "boom sections" are the lattice pieces that bolt/pin together like the fixed jib's; guy rods are the pull-rod chain to the tip, per the OEM Rod Plan drawing. A Liebherr part number is shown as a bonus cross-reference where confirmed against the parts catalogue — its absence doesn't mean anything about the code itself, which is already the OEM reference. The TN-TF adapter is required to attach either jib to the boom head and is listed on every length even though the OEM assembly drawing itself never calls it out.
